correctness.rationale: Direct composition of the two scalar component steps gives exactly \(X_{k+1}=(1-h)^2X_k\pm h^2b\). For \(0<h<2\) this is a strict affine contraction, so the unique invariant law is the convergent Rademacher series. The variance follows from independence. The support is the invariant set of two similarities: overlap occurs exactly at \(r\ge1/2\); at \(r<1/2\) the open-set condition gives the stated Hausdorff dimension and first-digit dominance gives the exact central gap. At \(r=1/2\), direct invariance of the uniform law proves the boundary distribution.

value.rationale: The defining constant-step random-reshuffling literature evaluates steady-state behavior mainly through mean-square error. The accepted result shows that second moments can hide a qualitatively different phenomenon: on a natural strongly convex two-sample problem the stationary epoch-start process can live on a disconnected fractal set with a positive gap around the exact minimizer, despite having zero mean. The complete transition from interval support to a uniform boundary law to Cantor support gives a natural sharp classification in the learning-rate parameter and supplies a concrete benchmark for distribution-level analyses of shuffling algorithms.
